svg.aria-label: How to write はい: 2 letters, は, い, one after another
svg.title: Writing はい
svg.desc: 2 letters written one after another: は, い (japanese). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansJP-Subset.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: は: KanjiVG, kanji/0306f.svg, hiragana は (U+306F HIRAGANA LETTER HA), three stroke paths kvg:0306f-s1 to s3 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/0306f.svg>; い: KanjiVG, kanji/03044.svg, hiragana い (U+3044 HIRAGANA LETTER I), two stroke paths kvg:03044-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/03044.svg>. Source notes on variation: は: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the left vertical drawn top to bottom, which turns at its foot and flicks up to the right without lifting; s2 is the bar drawn left to right; s3 starts above the bar, runs down through it, rounds to the left at its foot, comes back up, crosses the vertical and runs out to the lower right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. Where the print glyph's left vertical runs on below the point the flick leaves it, the path goes down to the foot of that ink and climbs back a short way before the flick. い: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 starts high on the left, comes down, curves round at its foot and flicks up to the right without lifting; s2 starts at the top of the short right stroke and runs down and slightly to the right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs.
svg.text: How it is written — 2 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 2 — 3 strokes · 2 pen lifts · 6 movements
Letter 2 of 2 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/0306f.svg, hiragana は (U+306F HIRAGANA LETTER HA), three stroke paths kvg:0306f-s1 to s3 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
Letter 2: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/03044.svg, hiragana い (U+3044 HIRAGANA LETTER I), two stroke paths kvg:03044-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
